text:
maria_support: Heads-up: getting a cluster of 503/504s from the inference gateway in eu-west-1 starting ~12:34UTC. Multiple customer reports of timeouts. Opening a containment thread. @jordan_oncall can you join?
kevin_sre: on it - I'm seeing a spike in upstream 5xx from the model-serving pool (svc-infer-eu). Error surface looks like gateway->runtime timeouts, not auth.
anna_prodeng: any correlation with the recent kernel/quant change we rolled two hours ago?
jordan_oncall: joining. logs show increased latency on kv-cache reads and a handful of connection resets from proxy pods. Pulling per-pod latencies now.
maria_support: customers A and B opened tickets, both timed out at ~30s and then got 502s. We're throttling new page loads in status page to avoid noise. Will notify customers in thread. :eyes:
kevin_sre: quick mitigations: 1) route traffic away from eu-west canaries to warm dedicated pools, 2) bump circuit-breaker threshold to avoid cascading retries, 3) restart the affected proxy replica set (graceful). Starting 1 and 2 now.
anna_prodeng: re: quant rollout - that was only on a small canary in prod-eu but should be isolated. I'll verify model variant tags to ensure fallback is available.
jordan_oncall: set cb threshold to 10s and enabled fallback to gpt-small-quantized variant for the critical endpoints. Re-routing completed at 12:43UTC.
ops-bot: deploy: proxy/rs restart initiated by kevin_sre at 12:45 UTC.
kevin_sre: restarted proxy pods, one pod failed readiness for ~1m then recovered. Post-restart traffic looks smoother but still elevated p50/p95. Keeping an eye on KV miss rate.
maria_support: FYI sent to affected customers with ETA 30m while we investigate.
anna_prodeng: KV cache miss rate jumped 4x at 12:34UTC, likely due to cache key eviction during burst. I'm going to increase cache TTL and warm top prefixes. Doing a controlled KV prewarm on the top 20 prompt prefixes.
jordan_oncall: prewarm kicked, p99 latency dropped from 3.2s to 1.1s on sample traffic. Still seeing sporadic 504s for long-running streams. Looks like some long-tail worker stalls.
kevin_sre: rolling a worker churn fix (adjust keepalive+max-conns) to the serving pool to mitigate stalls. Will monitor.
triage-bot: incident severity set to Sev-2 at 12:46 UTC.
maria_support: Customer comms updated to say "mitigation in progress, temporary fallback enabled, monitoring".
anna_prodeng: checklist for post-incident: (a) root-cause investigation on kv eviction pattern (b) increase probe coverage for worker stalls (c) evaluate autoscaling headroom and burst policies (d) add alert on rapid cache churn.
kevin_sre: agree. Also add a runbook step to toggle circuit-breaker thresholds per region and to warm fallbacks automatically if cache churn detected.
jordan_oncall: current status: 503 rate down to baseline, some residual 504 tail. Keeping the canary isolated and paused. I'll keep the thread updated; setting a follow-up postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 UTC.
maria_support: thanks team. I'm logging all customer tickets and next steps so CS can reference in postmortem.
kevin_sre: action items I'm owning: 1) investigate worker stall root cause (logs + core dumps) 2) add alert on proxy readiness flaps 3) revert risky kernel change if correlated.
anna_prodeng: action items I'm owning: 1) detailed KV cache telemetry (per-prefix) 2) automatic prewarm experiment for top prefixes 3) pull quant canary config and validate isolation.
jordan_oncall: I'll own the follow-up: postmortem doc, timeline, RCA, and customer impact summary.
maria_support: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups and prepare the incident summary for execs.
ops-bot: incident update: mitigations applied, monitoring for 30m window.
maria_support: closing note for the thread now: will reconvene in the postmortem meeting. If anything regresses, ping @jordan_oncall immediately. :thumbsup:
